welcome_message:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 Gold-layer data product — Databricks Asset Bundle + Azure DevOps CI/CD
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Answer 5 questions. Press Enter to accept the [default] shown in brackets.

product_name.description: 1/5 Product name (snake_case). Becomes the bundle name, the job names, and the prefix for tables this product creates. Lowercase letters, digits and underscores only. Example: sales_gold
product_name.pattern_match_failure_message: Use lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter (e.g. sales_gold).

workspace_host.description: 2/5 Workspace URL to deploy to, copied from your browser address bar. All three targets (dev/staging/prod) use this one workspace and are kept apart by schema. Must start with https://. Example: https://adb-1234567890123456.7.azuredatabricks.net
workspace_host.pattern_match_failure_message: Enter the full workspace URL, starting with https://

catalog.description: 3/5 Unity Catalog catalog where this product's tables live. It must already exist and you (plus the staging/prod service principals) must have access to it. Example: main
catalog.pattern_match_failure_message: A catalog name is letters, digits and underscores only.

schema.description: 4/5 Base schema name. dev and staging automatically get _dev and _staging added; prod uses the name as-is. So 'analytics' -> analytics_dev (dev), analytics_staging (staging), analytics (prod). Example: analytics
schema.pattern_match_failure_message: A schema name is letters, digits and underscores only.

warehouse_id.description: 5/5 SQL warehouse id used by dashboards and queries. Find it in the workspace: SQL Warehouses -> your warehouse -> the id in the page URL (or 'Connection details'). Leave blank if this product has no dashboard yet. Example: 862f1d757f0424f7
warehouse_id.pattern_match_failure_message: A warehouse id is letters and digits only (or leave blank).

success_message:
✅ Created bundle '{{.product_name}}'.

  Deploys to : {{.workspace_host}}
  Catalog    : {{.catalog}}
  Schemas    : {{.schema}}_dev (dev) | {{.schema}}_staging (staging) | {{.schema}} (prod)

Next steps:
  1. databricks bundle validate -t dev          # check it
  2. pip install -r tests/requirements.txt && pytest   # run unit tests (no cluster)
  3. Edit src/transformations.py + resources/   # replace the SAMPLE with your real logic
  4. git add . && git commit && git push        # the pipeline takes over from here
